correctness.rationale: Exact propagator and covariance verified from the drift matrix; the bath at Poisson epochs is a strictly contractive affine Gaussian recursion with a unique stationary perpetuity. Gaussian innovation exponential moments have sharp threshold sqrt(r(gamma+1)); a cosh Foster inequality proves finite bath moments below threshold. Stationary Poisson age mixing gives the same threshold for the reset tracer, with divergence at the endpoint. Chernoff and a long reset-free interval with bounded initial bath provide matching logarithmic tail exponents for both coordinates. Proof does not infer infinite tails from finite tests; extracted numerical verifier independently passed 387 checks.

value.rationale: For the same physically motivated selective-probe reset with a memory-retaining bath, the exact tail scale of both coordinates at finite bath friction is a natural rare-event observable unprovided by the parent mean-square/kurtosis analysis. It shows that large-friction Gaussian-looking central profiles hide exponential extreme tails at any finite friction, and supplies a parameter-exact decay length relevant to extreme excursion estimates. This is not a low-order normalization check or arbitrary finite slice.
